title: Hide the Meta AI button in WhatsApp
summary: A setting now exists to remove the blue circle from your chat list.
changes: The floating Meta AI button disappears and the AI chat leaves your list. Your messages and groups are untouched.
steps: Open WhatsApp and go to Settings.
Tap Chats.
Find "Show Meta AI Button" and switch it off.
If you do not see it, update WhatsApp — the setting is being rolled out gradually and arrives at different times in different countries.
how: Meta added the toggle after sustained complaints. It hides the entry point rather than removing the service from WhatsApp's servers.
caveats: Not everyone has the setting yet. If it is missing, you can still archive the Meta AI chat so it stays out of the way.
Meta AI can still be summoned inside a chat by typing @Meta AI. Simply don't.
Your ordinary messages remain end-to-end encrypted; only what you actively send to Meta AI goes to Meta.

alternatives.label: Move to a messenger with no assistant

title: Get Meta AI out of the way on Instagram and Facebook
summary: There is no off switch. There is, however, a reliable way to make it stop appearing.
changes: The Meta AI conversation is muted and archived, so it stops surfacing in your inbox and notifications.
steps: Open your direct messages.
Swipe or long-press the Meta AI conversation.
Choose Mute, then Archive or Delete. Deleting removes it from your list until you interact again.
In the search bar, ignore the AI suggestion row; it cannot currently be removed.
Turn off AI-related notifications: Settings → Notifications, and switch off anything mentioning Meta AI.
how: Meta treats its assistant as a contact rather than a feature, which is why there is no switch — but it also means the ordinary tools for unwanted contacts work on it.
caveats: The AI search suggestion inside the app cannot be hidden.
In the EU and UK you have a separate right to object to your public posts being used for training — see the next entry.

sources.title: How to turn off Meta AI

title: Object to your posts training Meta's AI
summary: In the UK and EU you can formally object, and Meta must honour it.
changes: Your public posts, photos and captions are excluded from Meta's generative AI training.
steps: Open Settings → Privacy Centre in the Facebook or Instagram app.
Find the notice about using your information for AI, or search Help for "object AI training".
Open the objection form and submit it. You do not have to give a reason in the EU or UK.
Repeat for each account. Facebook and Instagram are objected to separately unless they share an accounts centre.
how: European data protection law gives you a right to object to processing based on legitimate interest. Meta relies on that basis for training, so the objection has teeth.
caveats: Outside the EU, UK and a handful of other jurisdictions there is no equivalent right and no form.
Objecting does not remove data already used in models that have been trained.
Content other people have posted about you is not covered.

title: Stop X from feeding your posts to Grok
summary: One checkbox stops your posts and interactions being used to train Grok.
changes: Your posts stop being used for training. Grok remains in the app but stops learning from you.
steps: Open Settings → Privacy and safety.
Tap "Grok & third-party collaborators".
Uncheck "Allow your public posts as well as your interactions, inputs and results with Grok to be used for training and fine-tuning".
While you are there, use "Delete conversation history" to clear anything you have already sent to Grok.
how: X exposes this as a genuine account setting rather than a regional concession, so it works wherever you are.
caveats: It is easier to find on the website than in the mobile app.
It does not remove Grok's summaries from trending topics or the explore tab.
Setting your account to protected also removes your posts from training.

title: Stop LinkedIn training on your profile
summary: A direct link to the one switch that matters.
changes: Your profile, posts and activity stop being used to improve LinkedIn's generative AI models.
how: LinkedIn turned this on by default for most members. The switch is buried several levels deep in settings, so ILUD links straight to it.
caveats: It is not retroactive: data already used in trained models stays there.
LinkedIn's writing suggestions and profile rewrites are separate features you simply need not use.

sources.title: LinkedIn — Data for generative AI improvement

title: Read Reddit without the answer box
summary: Reddit Answers cannot be switched off, but a small add-on removes its links, and a plainer interface still exists.
changes: The generated answer prompts disappear from search and comment pages. Discussion threads read as they always did.
how: The add-on removes the Answers entry points from the page in your browser. It changes nothing on Reddit's side and sends nothing anywhere.
caveats: Reddit provides no setting to disable Answers.
old.reddit.com now requires you to be signed in and Reddit has said it is winding the old interface down, so do not rely on it.
Searching Reddit through Google with the Web filter is the most durable workaround and needs nothing installed.

title: Clear My AI from your Snapchat feed
summary: It cannot be deleted, but it can be unpinned and cleared out of the way.
changes: My AI stops sitting at the top of your chat list.
steps: Open the Chat screen.
Press and hold the My AI conversation.
Tap Chat Settings, then "Clear from Chat Feed".
Snapchat+ subscribers can also unpin it permanently.
caveats: It returns if you interact with it again.
Free accounts cannot remove it altogether; that is Snapchat's design, not an oversight on our part.

title: Reset a feed that has learned the wrong things
summary: Start the recommendation engine from scratch, or turn personalisation off entirely.
changes: Your For You feed forgets what it thought it knew and begins again from your new behaviour.
steps: Profile → menu → Settings and privacy.
Content preferences → Refresh your For You feed.
For a harder stop: Settings → Ads → Personalisation and data, and switch personalisation off.
On individual videos, long-press → Not interested.
caveats: Turning personalisation off makes the app considerably less useful; many people prefer the reset.
Menu names move between app versions.

title: Message on a platform with no assistant
summary: A messenger run by a non-profit, with no advertising, no AI features and no business model that needs them.
changes: Your conversations are end-to-end encrypted and there is no assistant in the app at all.
how: Signal is funded by donations through a non-profit foundation. It has no advertising business, and therefore no reason to build an assistant into your conversations.
caveats: Your correspondents have to be there too — that is the only real obstacle.
Requires a phone number to register, though usernames now hide it from contacts.

title: A feed in the order things happened
summary: Social networks where the timeline is chronological by design and nothing recommends anything.
changes: You see posts from people you follow, newest first. No ranking, no suggested accounts, no generated filler.
how: These networks are run by many independent servers rather than one company. Without an advertising market there is no incentive to reorder your timeline.
caveats: Choosing a server is an unfamiliar first step; any of the large general ones is fine and you can move later.
Smaller audiences. Good for conversation, less good for reaching strangers.

title: Put Facebook back in date order
summary: The chronological feed still exists, and you can bookmark it.
changes: Posts from friends and pages you follow, newest first, with no suggested content.
steps: On the website, the link above opens the most-recent view directly. Bookmark it.
In the app: tap the menu, then Feeds, then Friends or Favourites.
Add your favourite pages and people to Favourites so that feed is worth reading.
caveats: Facebook does not let you make this the default; you must go back to it each session.
The address form has changed before and may change again.

title: Know when a post was generated
summary: Every major platform now labels synthetic media. Learn where the label lives.
changes: You start noticing the small "AI info" or "AI-generated" marks that were always there.
steps: Instagram and Facebook: an "AI info" tag beneath the account name, or in the three-dot menu.
TikTok: an "AI-generated" sticker in the lower-left corner of the video.
YouTube: "Altered or synthetic content" in the expanded description.
If a post has no label but feels wrong, reverse-search a still from it.
how: Labels come from two sources: the uploader declaring it, and embedded provenance data written by the generating tool. Both are easy to strip, which is why the labels are a hint rather than a guarantee.
caveats: Absence of a label means nothing. Presence of one is reliable.
Re-uploads and screen recordings lose the embedded data.
